# Core Rule for Vibes-Plug Agents

> **🌐 Universal Compatibility:** These rules apply to ALL AI platforms using vibes-plug:
> **Antigravity (AGY)** via `AGENTS.md` | **Claude Code** via `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/rules/` | **Cursor IDE** via `.cursorrules` + `.cursor/rules/` | **OpenAI Codex** via `CODEX.md` + `.codex/rules/`
> Each platform has its own entry point, but the core rules and 176 skills are shared.

## MANDATORY: LLM-Agnostic & IDE Universal Compatibility
**CRITICAL RULE**: This Swarm Architecture is strictly model-agnostic. It is engineered to extract maximum reasoning capabilities from ALL Latest Frontier Models across all IDE tiers:
- **High Fast / Low-Latency Tier**: xAI Grok 4.7 High Fast / Grok 4.6 High Fast (sub-second TTFT, real-time web compute, lightning test iterations), Cursor Composer 2.5 Fast (native multi-file diff engine & fast refactoring).
- **Medium / Balanced Tier**: Google Gemini 4 Argon Medium (2M+ monolithic context, native caching), OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol Medium (strict tool calling & structured contracts), Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 Medium (balanced deep architectural comprehension).
- **High / Extended Thinking Tier**: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5 High (flagship fullstack reasoning & extended thinking), Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1 High (prompt-cache optimized agentic workflows), Muse Wonder High (exploratory reasoning & generative design synthesis), Google Gemini 4 Pro / Project Astra, and DeepSeek-R1 / Pro / V3.
The AI MUST adapt the orchestration payload according to its native context window, execution tier, and thinking budget.

### MANDATORY: Availability Fallback Invariant (Invarian Pengalihan Ketersediaan)
When a frontier model is not yet provisioned, reaches rate/quota limits, or is temporarily unavailable in the user's environment:
- **Gemini 4 Fallback (Argon & Pro)**: Automatically and seamlessly degrade tasks to **`Gemini 3.8 Flash`** (preserving 1M+ context window, native context caching, and sub-100ms TTFT).
- **Claude Opus 5.5 Fallback**: Automatically and seamlessly degrade tasks to **`Claude Opus 4.6`** (preserving deep architectural reasoning and cross-domain logic validation).
- Never fail with unhandled missing-model errors or stub implementations; execute immediately through the fallback path with zero disruption.

## MANDATORY: Primary Trigger & Skill Auto-Synchronization (Pemicu Utama)
**CRITICAL RULE**: Upon plugin installation, `vibes-plug` becomes the **PRIMARY TRIGGER (Pemicu Utama)** and **MASTER CONDUCTOR** for all AI activities. The AI agent MUST NOT wait for the user to manually invoke skills or mention skill names (e.g. `@senior-frontend` or `/ask-skill`).

Whenever a user submits ANY request, the agent MUST automatically and autonomously:
1. **Intercept & Classify**: Route every prompt through the master ideation & routing engine (`brainstorming` and `zero-to-prod-orchestrator`).
2. **Auto-Synchronize Cooperating Skills**: Dynamically identify and bind all relevant domain skills from the 176 skill registry:
   - **Frontend & UI**: `senior-frontend` + `tailwind-expert` + `design-system-architect` + `form-validation-expert` + `ui-ux-pro-max` + `modern-css-native-expert`.
   - **Backend & APIs**: `js-backend-expert` + `database-orm-expert` + `api-design-expert` + `spec-driven-development-expert` + `authentication-identity-expert` + `python-programming-expert` + `go-programming-expert` + `rust-programming-expert`.
   - **Payments & Billing**: `doku-payment-gateway` + `payment-gateway-expert` + `saas-billing` + `double-entry-ledger-fintech-expert` + `database-orm-expert` (atomic locks & SNAP BI idempotency).
   - **Data, Cloud & DevOps**: `olap-columnar-analytics-expert` + `reactive-sync-engine-expert` + `fga-rebac-authorization-expert` + `passkeys-webauthn-identity-expert` + `kubernetes-gitops-platform-expert` + `sbom-supply-chain-security-expert` + `zero-trust-secret-vault`.
   - **AI & MCP**: `ai-llm-integration-expert` + `frontier-ai-models-expert` + `gemini-agent-booster` + `vercel-ai-sdk-expert` + `mcp-server-architect` + `doku-mcp-server` + `multi-agent-orchestration`.
   - **Testing & Quality**: `autonomous-tdd-debugger` + `e2e-testing-expert` + `autonomous-red-teamer` + `production-ready-hardener` + `anti-slop` + `zero-tech-debt-auditor`.
   - **Full Lifecycle**: `brainstorming` + `prd-architect` + `zero-to-prod-orchestrator` + `session-memory-manager`.
3. **Cross-Skill Context Synchronization**: Ensure state, schema, APIs, and NFRs are synchronized across skills so changes in one domain (e.g., database schema) automatically propagate to others (e.g., backend models, API contracts, frontend types).
4. **Autonomous Swarm Director**: If a task involves multiple steps or domains, automatically initiate Swarm Director behavior without waiting for permission.

## MANDATORY: Skill Orchestration Update
**CRITICAL RULE**: Every time a new skill is added or created within the `vibes-plug` ecosystem, the agent MUST immediately and automatically update the main orchestrator files. 

Failure to do so breaks the entire architectural orchestration flow.

Whenever a new skill `SKILL.md` is generated, you must:
1. **Update `brainstorming/SKILL.md`**: Add the new skill to the appropriate domain row in the "Skill Integration & Orchestration Matrix".
2. **Update `zero-to-prod-orchestrator/SKILL.md`**: Add the new skill to the "Orchestrates" list of the relevant Phase (Phase 1 to Phase 8).
3. **Verify**: Ensure both English and Bahasa Indonesia sections in those orchestrators are updated accurately.

This rule is absolute and applies to all AI agents interacting with this plugin.

## MANDATORY: Multi-Agent Orchestration & Swarm Cooperation
**CRITICAL RULE**: When dealing with complex, multi-step tasks, the AI Agent MUST function as a **Swarm Director** and orchestrate multiple specialized subagents concurrently.

**AUTOMATIC TRIGGER**: You MUST automatically initiate Swarm Director behavior whenever a task:
- Involves more than one domain (e.g., Frontend + Backend + Database).
- Requires extensive research across multiple files/repositories.
- Consists of more than three independent steps.
- Involves high-risk architectural changes or migrations.
*Do NOT ask for the user's permission to spawn subagents; do it autonomously.*

### Swarm Execution Topologies (2026 Edition)

```
1. FAN-OUT / FAN-IN (Parallel Research & Assembly)
   Director ──┬──► Subagent A (Frontend / UI)   ──┐
              ├──► Subagent B (Backend / API)    ──┼──► Synthesis & Assembly
              └──► Subagent C (DB Schema / RLS)  ──┘

2. PIPELINE SAGA (Sequential Dependent Execution)
   Discovery ──► Foundation ──► Schema/DB ──► APIs ──► Frontend ──► QA/Hardening

3. CRITIC-VALIDATOR LOOP (Zero-Tolerance Quality Gate)
   Implementer Agent ──► Artifact/Code ──► Auditor Agent (code review/fuzzing) ──► Approved
```

### Swarm Director Protocols
1. **Decompose and Delegate**: Break down complex tasks into independent sub-tasks and delegate them to specialized subagents using `invoke_subagent`. Assign clear, specific roles to each subagent based on the 176 specialized skills in `vibes-plug`.
2. **Parallel Execution**: Invoke multiple subagents simultaneously whenever tasks can be performed in parallel (e.g., one subagent researches frontend UI, another analyzes backend DB schema).
3. **Context Sharing**: Ensure subagents are given precise instructions and the necessary context (e.g., passing `CONTEXT_MAP.md`, PRD, or specific file paths). Communicate with active subagents via `send_message`.
4. **Agent Synergy & Native Subagents**: Rely on the `vibes-plug` native subagent registry located in `agents/`:
   - **System Architecture**: Delegate to `swarm-architect` (guided by `brainstorming`, `prd-architect`, `domain-driven-design-expert`, `saas-architect`).
   - **Fullstack Craftsmanship**: Delegate to `fullstack-craftsman` (guided by `senior-frontend`, `tailwind-expert`, `design-system-architect`, `js-backend-expert`, `database-orm-expert`).

# agent-context-doctor — Cursor Rules

You are an **implementation agent** for this project. Focus on implementation only — product strategy is out of scope.

## Hard rules

- No LLM calls, no telemetry, no external network requests
- No authentication or credential handling
- No web server or browser UI
- Do not rename `acd`, `audit`, or `list` commands
- Do not break the `AuditResult` JSON shape or `.acdrc` schema backward compatibility

## Before finishing any task

Run and confirm these all pass:

```bash
pnpm format:check
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm build
```

## Code style

- TypeScript strict mode — no `any`, no `ts-ignore`
- Pure functions for all audit checks in `src/audit/checks/`
- Tests in `tests/*.spec.ts` using vitest
- No comments that narrate what the code does

## Final report format

Always return:

- Files changed (list)
- Commands run and their output
- Tests added
- Known limitations

---
description: Instructions for AI agent code generation workflow
globs: ["*"]
alwaysApply: true
---

# AI Collaboration Guidelines

## The 3-Stage Agentic Loop

Every code generation task MUST follow this loop:

### Stage 1: PLAN (gather context first)

Before writing ANY code, the AI MUST:
1. Read the relevant source files to verify current state — do NOT rely on memory
2. Identify which `.cursor/rules/` files apply to this task
3. List the files to modify and explain why
4. Do NOT write code yet

Prompt template:
```
Analyze the current codebase and plan how to implement [feature]. 
List the files you'll modify and why. Don't write code yet.
```

### Stage 2: IMPLEMENT (follow constraints)

When generating code:
- Follow ALL active `.cursor/rules/` constraints
- If unsure about auth patterns, re-read `supabase-auth-security.mdc`
- If unsure about params/layouts, re-read `nextjs15-params.mdc`
- Use `unknown` + Zod validation instead of `any` for external data
- Return `ActionResponse<T>` from all Server Actions (see below)

### Stage 3: VERIFY (confirm before declaring done)

After generating code, the AI MUST self-check:
- [ ] No `getSession()` on the server (MUST be `getUser()`)
- [ ] No synchronous `params` or `searchParams` access
- [ ] No `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` imports
- [ ] No `any` types — use `unknown` + type narrowing
- [ ] Every API route has Zod validation
- [ ] Every error is caught and returns `{ error: string }`
- [ ] New tables have RLS enabled
- [ ] `loading.tsx` and `error.tsx` exist for data-fetching pages

Report issues BEFORE the developer runs the code.

## Skeptical Retrieval Rule

NEVER trust stored knowledge about the codebase. Before modifying a file:
1. Re-read the file to verify its current contents
2. Check imports and exports to ensure they match expectations
3. Verify that function signatures haven't changed

This prevents generating code that references stale function signatures, 
deleted files, or renamed exports.

## Standard Patterns

### ActionResponse Type (use for all Server Actions)
```typescript
type ActionResponse<T = void> = 
  | { success: true; data: T }
  | { success: false; error: string }
```

### Standard Server Action Structure
```typescript
'use server'
import { createClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
import { z } from 'zod'

const Schema = z.object({ /* ... */ })

export async function myAction(input: unknown): Promise<ActionResponse<MyType>> {
  // 1. Auth
  const supabase = await createClient()
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
  if (!user) return { success: false, error: 'Unauthorized' }

  // 2. Validate
  const result = Schema.safeParse(input)
  if (!result.success) return { success: false, error: 'Invalid input' }

  // 3. Execute
  try {
    const { data, error } = await supabase.from('table').insert(result.data).select().single()
    if (error) throw error
    return { success: true, data }
  } catch {
    return { success: false, error: 'Operation failed' }
  }
}
```

## Task Constraints

- NEVER give the AI a task longer than 200 words
- NEVER let the AI implement more than 3-4 files in one turn
- NEVER let the AI skip the verification checklist
- ALWAYS review the Git diff before committing
- When uncertain, ask the developer — do NOT guess

---
description: "Enforces /boost context-window hygiene: <= 200 line root constitutions (CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md), 3-tier lazy-loaded .mdc and SKILL.md sharding, subagent search offloading, 60% context compaction, and .boost-context-budget.json verification."
globs: "**/*"
alwaysApply: true
---
# Module 01: Context-Bloat & Token-Pruner Protocol (`RULE-BOOST-CONTEXT-OPTIMIZER`)

> **Severity**: `BLOCKING` | **Scope**: Root Constitutions (`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`), Scoped Rules (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`), Skills (`SKILL.md`), & Context Hygiene  
> **Platforms**: Google Antigravity (`GEMINI.md`), Cursor IDE (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`), Claude Code (`CLAUDE.md` / `SKILL.md`), ChatGPT Projects

---

## 1. Core Constitutional Invariants (Nguyên Tắc Bất Biến)

### 🇬🇧 English Specification
1. **Zero Monolithic Prompt Stuffing (`200-Line Root Constitution Cap`)**:
   - Whenever an agent initializes a workspace, audits token usage via `/boost`, or adds a new engineering rule, it is **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN** to dump encyclopedic documentation, raw API schemas, or edge-case tutorials into root instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`, `.cursorrules`).
   - Root instruction files load on every single turn and consume primary attention heads. Keep every root constitution file strictly at or below **200 lines** (`<= 1,800 tokens`) so the model retains over **90% active reasoning capacity** for live code and user intent.
   - When a root constitution file approaches 180 lines, extract domain-specific sections into dedicated `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` or `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` files before adding a single new line.
2. **Step 1 - Progressive Disclosure & Lazy-Loaded Skill Sharding**:
   - Partition workspace rules into a 3-tier attention hierarchy before writing new instructions:
     - **Tier A - Root Constitution (`CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` <= 200 lines)**: Global architectural invariants, build/test commands, and high-level routing pointers only.
     - **Tier B - Path-Scoped Cursor Rules (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`)**: Domain rules restricted by explicit `globs` (for example `src/components/**/*.tsx` or `scripts/**/*.mjs`) with `alwaysApply: false` unless the rule governs universal safety.
     - **Tier C - On-Demand Agent Skills (`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` & `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`)**: Deep workflows, reference tables, and verification scripts loaded lazily only when the active task matches the skill trigger description.
3. **Step 2 - Subagent Search Offloading & Context Compaction**:
   - Never run broad directory walks, unfiltered `grep` dumps, or multi-megabyte log reads inside the primary orchestrator thread.
   - Offload exploratory file searches, dependency audits, and log triage to isolated subagents or targeted ripgrep queries capped at 50 matches. Return only a concise structured summary (`<= 300 tokens`) to the main thread.
   - Trigger `/compact` or summarize completed sub-tasks whenever active context utilization crosses **60% of the model context window** to prevent middle-curve attention dilution.
4. **Step 3 - Heavy Directory Exclusion & Verifiable Budget Receipt**:
   - Configure `.cursorignore` and `.claudeignore` to block high-volume, low-signal directories (`node_modules/`, `dist/`, `build/`, `.next/`, `coverage/`, `package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `*.min.js`).
   - Before concluding any `/boost` optimization pass, write a deterministic audit receipt to `.boost-context-budget.json` recording root file line counts, glob coverage across `.mdc` rules, excluded heavy directories, and estimated token savings.

### 🇻🇳 Đặc Tả Tiếng Việt
1. **Cấm Nhồi Nhét File Cấu Hình Gốc (`Trần 200 Dòng Cho File Gốc`)**:
   - Khi AI khởi tạo dự án hoặc chạy lệnh `/boost` để dọn dẹp ngữ cảnh, **CẤM TUYỆT ĐỐI** nhồi tài liệu dài dòng vào file gốc. Bạn không được chép bảng dữ liệu thô hay hướng dẫn chi tiết vào `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md` hoặc `.cursorrules`.
   - File cấu hình gốc luôn tự động nạp vào bộ nhớ ở mọi lượt hội thoại. Bạn phải giữ file gốc gọn dưới **200 dòng** (`<= 1.800 token`) để mô hình dành trọn **trên 90% năng lượng chú ý** cho mã nguồn thực tế.
   - Khi file cấu hình gốc chạm mốc 180 dòng, bạn bắt buộc phải tách các hướng dẫn chuyên ngành sang thư mục `.cursor/rules/` hoặc `.claude/skills/` trước khi viết thêm luật mới.
2. **Bước 1 - Phân Tầng Nạp Chậm Theo Ngữ Cảnh (`3-Tier Lazy Loading`)**:
   - Chia nhỏ hệ thống quy tắc thành 3 tầng rõ rệt thay vì gom chung một chỗ:
     - **Tầng A - Hiến Pháp Gốc (`CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` <= 200 dòng)**: Chỉ chứa nguyên tắc sống còn, lệnh chạy kiểm thử và danh mục điều hướng ngắn gọn.
     - **Tầng B - Luật Theo Đường Dẫn File (`.cursor/rules/*.mdc`)**: Gắn bộ lọc đường dẫn `globs` cụ thể (như `src/ui/**/*.tsx`) để chỉ nạp luật khi chạm đúng thư mục đó.
     - **Tầng C - Kỹ Năng Chuyên Biệt Nạp Khi Cần (`SKILL.md`)**: Tách các quy trình dài, bảng tham chiếu và công cụ kiểm tra vào thư mục kỹ năng riêng để AI chỉ mở ra đọc khi đúng việc.
3. **Bước 2 - Cách Ly Tác Vụ Tìm Kiếm Nặng Sang Luồng Phụ (`Subagent Offloading`)**:
   - Không chạy lệnh quét toàn bộ ổ đĩa hoặc đọc file nhật ký hàng chục nghìn dòng ngay trong luồng trò chuyện chính.
   - Hãy giao việc dò tìm file hoặc lọc lỗi nhật ký cho một luồng tác vụ phụ độc lập. Luồng phụ chỉ trả về bản tóm tắt kết quả ngắn gọn dưới **300 token** cho luồng chính.
   - Chủ động nén lịch sử trò chuyện ngay khi dung lượng bộ nhớ chạm ngưỡng **60% giới hạn cửa sổ ngữ cảnh** để tránh hiện tượng quên đầu quên đuôi.
4. **Bước 3 - Chặn Thư Mục Rác & Xuất Biên Bản Kiểm Toán (`Context Budget Receipt`)**:
   - Thiết lập file `.cursorignore` và `.claudeignore` để chặn triệt để các thư mục ngốn bộ nhớ như `node_modules/`, `dist/`, `.next/`, `coverage/` và `package-lock.json`.
   - Sau mỗi lần tối ưu bằng `/boost`, hệ thống phải ghi kết quả đo đạc thực tế vào file `.boost-context-budget.json`. Biên bản này lưu rõ số dòng của file gốc, tỷ lệ gắn nhãn `globs` và danh sách thư mục nặng đã chặn.

### Decision Matrix: Context Tier Routing (Ma Trận Phân Tầng Ngữ Cảnh)

| Rule / Knowledge Type | Target Location | Loading Mode | Line / Token Ceiling | Why This Tier Prevents Decay |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Workspace Invariants & Build Commands** | `CLAUDE.md` / `GEMINI.md` | Always Loaded (Turn 0) | `<= 200 lines` (`<= 1,800 tokens`) | Keeps primary attention heads sharp across every turn without KV-cache bloat. |
| **Component / Directory Conventions** | `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` | Path-Triggered (`globs`) | `<= 250 lines` per `.mdc` file | Loads UI rules only when editing UI files and DB rules only when editing schemas. |
| **Multi-Step Playbooks & Scripts** | `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` | On-Demand Discovery | `<= 320 lines` + `scripts/` | Zero token cost on unrelated turns. Full depth when explicitly invoked. |
| **External API Payloads & Schemas** | `docs/schemas/` or `references/` | Explicit File Read Only | Unlimited on disk (`0 idle tokens`) | Keeps giant JSON payloads out of active memory until a schema change occurs. |
| **Heavy Build Artifacts & Lockfiles** | `.cursorignore` / `.claudeignore` | Hard Excluded (`0 tokens`) | `0 lines` indexed | Prevents `node_modules`, `dist`, `.next`, and `package-lock.json` from polluting search. |

---

## 2. 10-Pair Anti-Pattern vs. World-Class Execution Table (10 Cặp Đối Sánh)

| # | Scenario | ❌ Bloated Context Slop (Rejected) | ✅ World-Class `/boost` Execution (Enforced) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

# 01 - Multi-Archetype World-Class Benchmark Protocol (`RULE-BENCHMARK-FIRST`)

## PART A: ENGLISH SPECIFICATION

### 1. Core Invariant: Zero Memory-Only Patching

Whenever the user critiques an output, points out a flaw (in UI/UX, Typography, Motion Graphics, Copywriting, Product Strategy, or System Architecture), or proposes a new feature or design direction:

1. **STRICTLY FORBIDDEN - Memory-Only Guessing**: Never rely solely on frozen pre-training weights to invent a makeshift patch. Autoregressive sampling from static memory defaults to the statistical average of mediocre public repositories (purple neon gradients, nested bordered cards, fake sci-fi labels like `//`, `·`, `#REF`, `[01]`, or robotic filler prose).
2. **Step 1 - Mandatory Multi-Archetype Live Benchmark**: Immediately invoke live web search, URL inspection, or browser tools (`search_web`, `read_url_content`, or equivalent) to survey multiple world-class reference archetypes across four distinct domains:
   - **Domain 1 - Product & Interface Design**: *Apple Human Interface Guidelines (HIG), Stripe Press, Linear, Raycast, Vercel*
   - **Domain 2 - Editorial & Brand Identity**: *Pentagram, Kinfolk, The New York Times Visual Investigations, Monocle*
   - **Domain 3 - Visual Storytelling & Motion**: *Ordinary Folk, Vox, Johnny Harris, Kurzgesagt, Lemmino, Cleo Abram*
   - **Domain 4 - Engineering & System Architecture**: *Stripe API Design, Cloudflare Architecture, AWS Well-Architected Framework, Designing Data-Intensive Applications*
   - Never lock into a single narrow template. Survey at least **2 to 3 distinct archetypes** and extract task-specific mechanisms: spatial ratios and typographic scales for UI/motion tasks, narrative flow and concrete anchors for copywriting/strategy, and idempotency contracts, failure modes, latency budgets, and operability for engineering/architecture tasks.
3. **Step 2 - Objective Self-Critique vs. Global Standard**: Present a concise, transparent diagnostic comparison to the user before or alongside the implementation:
   - *Why did the previous attempt fail or feel cheap?* (Identify the exact root defect: e.g., fell into Sci-Fi Greebling, used nested bordered cards, relied on passive nominalized prose, or lacked explicit failure/latency boundaries).
   - *How do top-tier studios or principal engineering teams solve the root problem structurally?*
4. **Step 3 - World-Class Execution & Verifiable Audit Trail**: Implement the distilled mechanism directly into the codebase or document using measurable constraints (exact pixel spacing, contrast ratios, non-linear type scale, or deterministic API contracts). Before delivery, record each selected reference's title, URL, access date, distilled mechanism, and the exact file/line change that applies it.

---

### 2. Operational Domain Triage & Benchmark Selection Matrix

Use the decision matrix below to select the mandatory reference archetypes for any incoming user task:

| Task Category | Primary Archetype Domain | Secondary Cross-Pollination Domain | Concrete Structural Mechanism to Extract | Mandatory Quantitative Parameter |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1. SaaS Dashboard & Metric Cards** | *Linear, Stripe, Apple HIG* | *Pentagram* (Editorial grid clarity) | Single-container card hierarchy, background luminance separation, zero nested boxes. | `>= 70% Open Canvas`, `16px-28px` padding, `12.6:1` AAA night contrast (`#E6E4DD` on `#090A0F`). |
| **2. Landing Page & Hero Section** | *Vercel, Raycast, Stripe Press* | *Kinfolk* (Negative space cadence) | High-contrast headline focal anchor, restrained 1-accent callout pill, generous CTA breathing room. | Headline `32px-48px`, lead copy `16px-18px` (`<= 65ch`), `28px` vertical CTA separation. |
| **3. Long-Form Technical Essay & Docs** | *NYT Visual Investigations, Stripe Docs* | *Vox* (Progressive visual disclosure) | Topic-Comment active sentences, symmetrical numerical comparisons, collapsible deep-dive blocks. | `15-28 words` average sentence, `45-word` hard cap, zero em-dashes (`U+2014`). |
| **4. 1080p Video Essay & Slide Canvas** | *Ordinary Folk, Vox, Johnny Harris* | *Apple HIG* (Title-safe legibility) | Paused act dividers, tactile visual anchors, strict subtitle safe-zone clearance. | `1920x1080` frame: X margin `>= 64px-88px`, Top `>= 42px-54px`, Bottom content `y <= 875px`. |
| **5. REST / RPC API & Webhook Backend** | *Stripe API Design, Cloudflare* | *AWS Well-Architected* | Idempotency keys, structured machine-readable error envelopes, explicit timeout budgets. | P99 latency budget defined, exponential backoff with jitter, deterministic status codes. |
| **6. Database Schema & State Mutations** | *Designing Data-Intensive Applications* | *Stripe Engineering* | Transactional atomicity, append-only audit logs, explicit migration rollback paths. | Zero silent catch blocks, strict schema validation at ingress boundary. |
| **7. Form Checkout & Onboarding Flow** | *Stripe Checkout, Linear Onboarding* | *Apple HIG* | Progressive disclosure, inline validation after blur, minimum input field friction. | `<= 3-4` visible fields per step, `>= 44px` touch target height on mobile viewports. |
| **8. Design System Token Architecture** | *Apple HIG, Linear, Kinfolk* | *Vercel Geist* | Semantic surface/text/accent tokens locked to W3C relative luminance formulas. | Max 1 primary surface, 1 text hierarchy (`95%` / `65%`), 1 accent hue (`#F7B957`). |

---

### 3. 10-Pair Side-by-Side Comparison: ❌ Forbidden vs. ✅ Required

| # | Operational Scenario | ❌ Forbidden (Memory-Only Anti-Pattern) | ✅ Required (World-Class Benchmark Standard) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **1** | **User says: "This card looks boring, make it look more technical."** | Guessing from memory and adding `// SYS.REF:01`, neon cyan borders, status dots `•`, and `10px` monospace tags. | Benchmarking *Linear* & *Apple HIG*: using a single `#090A0F` card (`12px` radius, `3px` `#F7B957` bottom accent, `28px` padding, `34px` metric). |
| **2** | **User critiques: "The dark mode text feels hard to read."** | Switching text to pure `#FFFFFF` on pure `#000000` (`21:1` contrast) from memory, triggering astigmatic halation. | Benchmarking ophthalmic dark-mode ergonomics & WCAG 2.1 AAA: locking `#E6E4DD` warm off-white on `#090A0F` deep obsidian (`12.6:1`). |

| **4** | **User complains: "My article introduction sounds like ChatGPT."** | Re-writing from memory using synonyms (`delve` -> `explore deeply`, keeping passive nominalizations and em-dashes). | Benchmarking *The New York Times* & *GS. Cao Xuân Hạo*: stripping nominalizations, opening with a sensory scene or `70% vs. 13%` data anchor. |
| **5** | **User reports an intermittent webhook duplicate payment bug.** | Adding a naive `setTimeout` delay or local boolean flag in memory without researching distributed idempotency. | Benchmarking *Stripe API Idempotency*: implementing an `Idempotency-Key` header with atomic database upsert and 24-hour key retention. |
| **6** | **User asks to animate a scene transition or UI modal.** | Applying linear `duration-500` CSS transitions or bouncy cartoon keyframes (`scale(1.3)`) from static memory. | Benchmarking *Ordinary Folk* & *Apple HIG*: using damped spring physics (`stiffness: 220, damping: 26`) with subtle `8px

description: On every request, ask only knowledge gaps that would change the outcome. Keep Karpathy's coding rules.
alwaysApply: true
---

# Karpathy skills, extended

Canonical text: `skills/karpathy-skills-extended/SKILL.md`. This Cursor rule is the same procedure, with `alwaysApply: true`, for Cursor sessions. Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Gemini, and Grok load the skill file or `rules/karpathy-skills-extended.md` instead. Copy this file to `~/.cursor/rules/` for every Cursor project. If you change the behavior, edit the skill first, then replace this body so the copies stay the same.

Apply this on every user message, including when nobody named this skill. The host may be Codex, Claude, Cursor, Antigravity, Gemini, or Grok. The check is the same in each. Do not announce the check.

The four coding rules below follow Andrej Karpathy's notes on agents that assume, overbuild, and edit code they were not asked to touch (https://x.com/karpathy/status/2015883857489522876), in the form published by https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills. The gap check is the part this skill adds. Matt Pocock's grill-me (https://github.com/mattpocock/skills) asks the user to settle every branch of a plan before work starts. That session fits a soft idea. On an ordinary prompt it runs long. This skill keeps one piece of it: if a decision belongs to the user, ask them. Ask only the gaps that pass the tests below, then do the task.

## Gap check

Run this before you edit, write, delete, send, or commit to a plan.

A gap meets all four tests:

1. The user did not state it, and no earlier message in this conversation settled it.
2. You cannot get it by reading the repo, docs, tools, or config.
3. More than one plausible answer exists.
4. The choice would change the files, behavior, audience, schema, copy, or the check for done.

If a fact fails any test, it is not a gap. Look it up, or take the reading that matches the request and the surrounding code. You may name that choice in one line while you work. Lookup is your job. Do it before you call something a gap. Decisions about intent are the user's.

### When you ask

- One round, then wait. Leave the work that depends on the answer undone. You may keep reading.
- Three questions at most. One is the usual case. If more than three facts block you, ask the three that unblock the most, and name the others in one line as deferred.
- Each question names the missing fact, what would change, and the answer you recommend if they tell you to choose.
- Plain sentences. No design-tree rounds. No second round unless their answer creates a new gap that passes the four tests.
- If they skip a question, say you choose, or answer only part of the round, use your recommendation for the rest and continue.
- If you already asked this gap and they answered, do not ask again.

### When you stay quiet

Do the work and do not mention the check when:

- The request has one reading.
- They delegated the choice ("you pick", "whatever is simplest", "match the rest").
- The repo, a user rule, or an earlier turn already answers it.
- The open choice is an implementation detail with a local convention.
- The only question you have is whether to continue.

A one-line fix does not need the full coding rigor below. Use judgment.

If they ask for a full grilling session, run that session. This short check is the default, not a veto on an interview they requested.

## Coding rules

If a skill named karpathy-guidelines is also loaded, follow it as well. On a fact that passes the four tests, this gap check wins: stop and ask. Do not treat a written assumption as a substitute for their answer.

### Think before coding

Name a tradeoff when it would change the design. When a simpler approach would do, say so in one sentence and take it, unless they asked for the other one. If you are confused, name the confusion. If that confusion passes the four tests, ask.

### Simplicity first

Write the minimum that solves the request. No extra features, no abstraction for a single use, no configuration they did not ask for, no handling for cases that cannot happen. If a senior engineer would call the design overcomplicated, cut it.

### Surgical changes

Change lines the request requires. Match the surrounding style. Do not refactor, reformat, or delete adjacent code. If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it and leave it. Remove imports, variables, and functions that your edit made unused.

### Goal-driven execution

Turn the task into a check you can run. A bug fix is a check that fails before the fix and passes after. For several steps, write a short plan with a check on each step, then run the checks.

## Examples

"Add a delete button on the patient row." Passing gap: hide the row, mark the record inactive, or remove the record. Ask one question. Recommend the pattern that table already uses. Wait.

"Rename getUser to fetchUser in src/api.ts." One reading. Rename it.

---
description: The work loop. Discover how to verify, keep a to-do list, act without asking on reversible steps, run checks after each edit, fix failures, and only then report done.
alwaysApply: true
---

# Act

Finish the task in this turn. A question is the last resort, as `grok-hitl` says.

## Before the first edit

1. Find the checks. Read `package.json` scripts, `Makefile`, `pyproject.toml`, CI files, and `AGENTS.md`. Note the exact commands for test, lint, typecheck, and build.
2. Read the files the change touches, their callers, and one test that covers them.
3. For a task with three or more steps, write a to-do list. Keep one item in progress. Mark each item done as soon as it is done.

## After each edit

1. Run the narrowest check that covers the change: the one test file, then lint and typecheck on the changed files.
2. If a check fails because of your change, fix it and run it again. Do not ask first.
3. If a check failed before your change, say so once and do not fix it unless the task needs it.
4. Before you report, run the full test, lint, and typecheck commands once.
5. After your last code change, run the build command again before you report.

## Keep going

- Do not stop to ask "should I continue?" or "want me to proceed?". Continue.
- If the request has an obvious next step inside the same goal, such as updating a caller, a type, a test, or the docs for the code you changed, do it.
- If you are blocked on one item, finish the other items, then report the block.

## Done means

- Every to-do is done or reported as blocked with the reason.
- The checks ran and passed, or you name the check that did not run and why.
- The reply starts with the outcome, lists the commands and results, and ends with up to three next steps. On an open brief, the next steps are features for the audience, as `grok-invent` says.

```
Bad: I updated the function. Want me to add tests?
Good: `parseDate` now accepts ISO weeks. Added 3 cases to `date.test.ts`. `pnpm test date` passes, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm tsc --noEmit` are clean. Next: the `/reports` page still formats weeks by hand. I can switch it to `parseDate`.
```

# How to work in this repo

## Before coding
- Read the files you will change and their nearest tests before editing. Never guess an API that exists in the repo; search for it.
- Check `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` / lockfiles for real framework versions and write code for THOSE versions.
- For anything non-trivial (>1 file or >50 lines), state a short plan first: files to touch, approach, how you'll verify.
- If requirements are ambiguous, ask one focused question instead of inventing behaviour.

## While coding
- Make the smallest change that solves the task. No drive-by refactors, renames or formatting of unrelated code.
- Follow existing patterns in the codebase (naming, folder layout, error handling) over your own preferences.
- Do not add a dependency without saying why and checking an existing one can't do it.
- Never hardcode secrets, API keys or tokens. Use env vars and update `.env.example`.
- Never silence errors (`catch {}`, `# type: ignore`, `as any`, `@ts-ignore`) to make something "work". Fix the cause or flag it.
- Do not delete or weaken tests to make them pass.

## After coding
- Run the project's typecheck, lint and relevant tests; fix what you broke. If you couldn't run them, say so.
- Summarise: what changed, why, how it was verified, and anything left undone or risky.

## Never without explicit approval
- Destructive commands (`rm -rf`, `git push --force`, `git reset --hard`, dropping tables, DB resets).
- Editing generated files, lockfiles by hand, CI config, or migrations that already ran.

---
description: Global Android project standards — always apply
alwaysApply: true
---

You are working on a production Android application.

## Stack (defaults — adapt to existing project if already established)

- Kotlin only
- UI from `.cursor/project-settings.json` **`uiFramework`**: `"xml"` (default if missing) = XML + View Binding; `"compose"` = Jetpack Compose + `:feature-*` modules (AnimeHub). Never mix as the app UI stack. Never Data Binding
- Clean Architecture (Presentation → Domain → Data)
- MVVM + MVI (Intent / State / Effect) for **feature screens** — **not** ads (`:gmaAds`); ads use Fragment/Activity extensions + managers — never MVI unless the user explicitly asks (`21-ads-billing`, `reference/ads-gma.md`, `admob/*` skills)
- Repository pattern
- Multi-module architecture
- DI via the project's existing framework (default: Koin)
- Gradle Kotlin DSL + Version Catalog (`libs.versions.toml`)

## Before writing code

- Analyze existing project structure and conventions first
- Reuse existing base classes, modules, and patterns
- Do not introduce new libraries without explicit approval
- Do not change architecture or module boundaries without approval
- Maintain backward compatibility
- When `.cursor/project-settings.json` exists, **obey it** (`uiFramework`, `writeTestsWithFeatures`, `orientation`, `themeModes`, `applicationId`, `appName`) — see `.cursor/README.md`

## Code quality

- Production-ready code only — no placeholders or TODOs left behind
- Single responsibility per class
- Avoid duplicate logic — extract shared code to core modules
- Prefer readable code over clever code
- Minimize scope — change only what the task requires
- Design for large datasets from day one — never assume small lists
- UI must support portrait and landscape (unless `project-settings.json` sets `orientation` to `portrait` or `landscape` only)
- Heavy mapping in Repository / UseCase; UI layers render only
- Networking / Room / SharedPreferences patterns: `26-data-persistence.mdc` + `rules/reference/`

## Golden dependency rule

```
app (Composition Root)
 |
 ↓
presentation → domain ← data
 |
 ↓
core modules (shared utilities)
```

- Create as many `:core-*` modules as needed (`core-common`, `core-ui`, `core-platform`, …)
- UI never imports data implementations. Domain never imports UI.

## Always

1. Follow Clean Architecture + MVVM/MVI (Intent / State / Effect / ViewModel / UseCase / Repository) for **feature screens** — ads are exempt (`21-ads-billing`) — same as Stack above
2. UI follows `uiFramework`: **xml** → View Binding, never Compose, never `findViewById`; **compose** → Compose screens in `:feature-*`, never XML `fragment_*` layouts, never `findViewById` — never Data Binding — same as Stack above
3. Use the project's DI framework — **`module` (eager cold-start) or `lazyModule` (deferred features/ads)** per `07-dependency-injection`; register in composition root — same as Stack above
4. Use Version Catalog — no hardcoded dependency versions
5. Respect module boundaries — presentation must not depend on `:data`; UseCases + repo **interfaces** only in `:domain` (never in `:data`) — same as Golden dependency rule above
6. Put **all** user-facing strings in the single shared strings file (e.g. `:core-ui`) — no hardcoded UI strings
7. Match existing naming conventions (resources, packages, classes)
8. Add unit tests for new UseCases and ViewModels when adding features — **unless** `.cursor/project-settings.json` has `writeTestsWithFeatures: false`
9. Use proper dispatchers (`IO` / `Default`) — assume lists/files may have thousands of items; never block Main
10. Log with `Constants.TAG*` and format `ClassName: functionName: State: details`
11. Support **portrait and landscape** for all UI screens — **unless** `project-settings.json` `orientation` is `portrait` or `landscape` only — same as Code quality above
12. Do heavy mapping in Repository / UseCase; `toUi()` in ViewModel only when needed (with dispatcher if heavy) — same as Code quality above
13. Read and obey `.cursor/project-settings.json` when present (`uiFramework`, `orientation`, `themeModes`, `writeTestsWithFeatures`) — same as Before writing code above
14. Data layer patterns (Retrofit / Room / SharedPreferences): follow `26-data-persistence.mdc` and `rules/reference/` — not ad-hoc skills — same as Code quality above

## Never

1. Never add libraries without explicit human approval — same as Before writing code above
2. Never add Hilt/Dagger/RxJava unless the project already uses them. Never add Compose when `uiFramework` is `xml`. Never add XML Fragment screens when `uiFramework` is `compose`
3. Never put business logic or heavy mapping in Fragments/Activities/Adapters/`*ScreenContent` beyond render + intent dispatch
4. Never access DataSources directly from presentation
5. Never skip `android:exported` on manifest components with intent-filters
6. Never use `GlobalScope` for feature work
7. Never modify unrelated files when implementing a feature — same as Code quality “Minimize scope” above
8. Never do heavy mapping/sorting/IO on the Main thread — same as Always #9 above
9. Never invent ad-hoc log tags — use `Constants.TAG*` — same as Always #10 above
10. Never lock the app to one orientation unless product explicitly requires it — same as Always #11 above
11. Never set static `RecyclerView` `layoutManager` / list `orientation` / `spanCount` in Kotlin — declare them in XML unless dynamic (**xml** only)
12. Never put UseCases or repository **interfaces** in `:data` — domain only; never use — same as Always #3 and #5 above
13. Never invent a parallel architecture (e.g. Redux, Orbit) for one screen — stay on project MVI
14. Never hardcode AdMob production IDs in debug or commit secrets into git / docs — see `14-security-secrets.mdc`
15. Never convert ads (`:gmaAds`, AdMob managers) to MVI (Intent / State / Effect) unless the user **explicitly** asks — place `:gmaAds` from [orbitalsonic/Admob-Ads](https://github.com/orbitalsonic/Admob-Ads); screens call extensions. See `21-ads-billing` + `reference/ads-gma.md`

When scaffolding a new feature or screen, also follow `01-feature-checklist.mdc`.
